docs.title: Welcome to NebulaLE
docs.text:
NebulaLE (Nebula Low Energy) is a continuation of the Nebula simulator of electron-matter interaction, with specific focus on improving the simulator and its physics models to work better at low electron energies (< 100 eV).

The original Nebula simulator can be found on github, and its documentation is here. The basic functionality of the simulator has been explained there and will not be repeated here.

The main repository for NebulaLE can be found at: NebulaLE

The associated repository for cstoolLE is: cstoolLE.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
There are currently 5 commands one can run in order to use NebulaLE:

  • nebula_gpu

  • nebula_cpu_mt

  • nebula_cpu_edep

  • nebula_cpu_traj

  • nebula_cpu_SE_mode

docs.title: GPU version: nebula_gpu
docs.text: Run Nebula on the GPU. Not all changes in NebulaLE are guaranteed to work for GPU, so use of this version is not recommended.

docs.title: CPU main version: nebula_cpu_mt
docs.text: Run Nebula on the CPU. This is the standard version of Nebula.

docs.title: CPU edep version: nebula_cpu_edep
docs.text:
Run Nebula on the CPU, with a custom output datatype that logs energy deposition events. Detection events (if detector is present) are stored in a .bin file instead of a .det file.

The output datatype is given by:

import numpy as np

energy_dtype = np.dtype([ 
('x', '=f'), 
('y', '=f'), 
('z', '=f'), # Position 
('E', '=f'), # Energy of electron before collision at position x, y, z (in eV) 
('dE', '=f'), # Energy loss (deV) 
('px', '=i'), # Pixel x of initial primary beam electron 
('py', '=i')]) # Pixel y of initial primary beam electron

(Current bug: total energy outputted is too high: Secondary electron energy is double counted.)

docs.title: CPU trajectories version: nebula_cpu_traj
docs.text:
Run Nebula on the CPU, with a custom output datatype that logs every single event that the electron encounters (inelastic, elastic, boundary crossing (transmission and reflection), mirroring (against a mirror plane), detection, termination. IDs of each event type are custom, and require a special script to interpret.

The output datatype is given by:

import numpy as np

trajectory_dtype = np.dtype([ 
('x', '=f'), 
('y', '=f'), 
('z', '=f'), # Position 
('E', '=f'), # Energy of electron before collision at position x, y, z (in eV) 
('dE', '=f'), # Energy loss (deV) 
('px', '=i'), # Pixel x of initial primary beam electron 
('py', '=i'), # Pixel y of initial primary beam electron 
('tag', '=i'), # Unique ID tag of initial primary beam electron  
('ns', '=i')]) # Consecutive scattering event number

(Current bug: blocks GPU compilation, there seem to be some inelastic events missing in the list of output events.)

docs.title: CPU SE version: nebula_cpu_SE_mode
docs.text:
Run Nebula on the CPU, with an additional output of the scatter counter. This is distinct from the trajectories version because it focuses on detected electrons and not "events" in general.

The output datatype is given by:

import numpy as np

SE_mode_dtype = np.dtype([ 
('x', '=f'), 
('y', '=f'), 
('z', '=f'), # Position 
('dx', '=f'), 
('dy', '=f'), 
('dz', '=f'), # Direction 
('E', '=f'), # Energy 
('sc', '=i'), # Scatter counter 
('px', '=i'), 
('py', '=i')]) # Pixel index

(Current bug: blocks GPU compilation)
